answer:
Yes—as a design judgment, this addresses the demonstrated failure, provided “fits the viewport” means fits the actual text area after persistent chrome and any continuation banner. It also honestly bounds oversized paragraphs rather than pretending to solve their semantics. I would tighten the contract in a few places, not change the approach.

Evidence: I recovered the September 9, 2026 review at @session:default/run_428b76d21a4e427487d187b60a549e14. It identified case-c-80x24-end.txt displaying “actual identifier is supplied for this fictional example.” after scrolling “no” out of view. That review examined supplied artifacts, not on-disk originals. I have not inspected the proposed implementation or new test results.

For that specific failure, keeping the fitted detail’s beginning visible prevents the clipped affirmative fragment. Numbered identity and connectors can remain; neither caused the loss of negation. No author shortening or natural-language inference is needed.

My recommended refinements are engineering details, not additional established requirements.

First, define one legal-position rule shared by j/k, page movement, preview offsets, End, and resize/reflow. Otherwise a corrected keyboard path can coexist with the same failure through an arbitrary preview offset or a narrower terminal. Measure paragraph heights using the rendered width and effective text height. Account for banner space without allowing banner appearance to make fit classification oscillate.

Second, distinguish protecting the top edge from making every visible paragraph complete. Boundary snapping prevents a fitted paragraph from beginning mid-sentence at the top. It does not prevent a later paragraph from being cut at the bottom, before a qualification. For the smallest correction, explicitly mark a cut-off bottom paragraph as continuing below. Your proposed “earlier text above” warning is appropriate only when earlier text is actually hidden; oversized paragraphs also need a truthful “continues below” state. Neither warning guarantees correct interpretation, but both disclose incompleteness. If you instead promise whole fitted paragraphs everywhere, you must defer a paragraph that cannot fit the remaining space, leaving blank rows. That is a stronger policy than the demonstrated fix requires.

Third, make overlap a preference, not an unconditional page-navigation requirement. If one paragraph fills the text area, the next boundary may provide no overlap. Require forward progress without skipping unread text; overlap where possible. Also qualify End: use a paragraph boundary when the remaining tail fits, but permit an explicitly marked interior position when the final paragraph itself is oversized. Otherwise the proposed End rule has no solution in that case.

The honest remaining limit is slightly broader than oversized paragraphs: paragraph boundaries are structural, not proof of semantic independence. A complete detail can still depend on its label or a preceding paragraph. Persistent item identity helps readers locate context; it does not carry that context’s meaning. Keep the existing qualification-placement expectations, but describe this correction as preventing unmarked leading truncation of fitted paragraphs—not guaranteeing self-contained meaning.

For verification, I would expect the exact “no actual identifier” regression exercised through every positioning path, plus effective-height edge cases, resize/reflow, an oversized final paragraph, and page movement without skipped text. These would be post-trial engineering regression tests, not a rerun of the independent author experiment.

My recommendation is to proceed with boundary snapping and explicit directional continuation disclosure. I do not see a smaller equally reliable correction for the demonstrated fitted-paragraph failure. The remaining product choice is whether bottom-edge disclosure suffices or fitted paragraphs must always be shown whole; that belongs to Travis/PO. The frozen trial remains evidence of the original failure, and this advice is neither implementation verification nor PO approval.
note: Dottie evidence/context, not implementation authorization. No automatic retry.
